clue.text: Drink for an Oxford Street dance

parts.note: the main street of Oxford is the High, short for High Street
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone picks a drink to fuel a night of dancing in an Oxford street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford Street' suggests the London shopping street, but here it is Oxford's own main street, known simply as the High.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mixed spirit served with soda and ice in a long glass is called by this name.

clue.text: I say, hark to the evolutionary theorist

parts.note: ho is an exclamation to call attention, like 'I say!'
list is an old word meaning listen, as hark does

explanation.surface: A cry to listen to a lecturer on evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Holism, Jan Smuts's theory that wholes evolve beyond the sum of their parts, is the theory meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in holism, Smuts's evolutionary theory that nature tends to form wholes.

clue.text: Cutting Thanksgiving shows lack of decency

definitions.note: noun phrase for an adjective; with 'shows' it describes someone lacking decency

parts.note: grace is a prayer of thanks before a meal
less means without, as when something is cut out

explanation.surface: Skipping the prayer before dinner is a sign of bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' a thing leaves you without it, so cutting grace is being grace-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without manners or refinement is crude, lacking any courtesy.

clue.text: Fragile association of the Britains with the French

parts.note: BRITT, with the T doubled for a plural, abbreviates Britanniarum, 'of the Britains', on British coins
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A shaky alliance between the British peoples and France.
explanation.walkthrough: British coins carried BRITT for 'of the Britains', the doubled letter marking the plural, as in a monarch's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle is easily snapped, so it is delicate and breakable.

clue.text: Refreshment in a trekker's encampment, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a laager is a Boer camp formed by a ring of wagons on the trek

explanation.surface: A drink is served at camp after a long trek.
explanation.walkthrough: The trekkers are Boer pioneers in South Africa, whose wagon-circle camp was a laager.
explanation.definitionFit: A light beer is a common drink to refresh oneself.

clue.text: Loved an artist in our time

indicators.note: the artist's name sits within the letters standing for our time

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator and engraver

explanation.surface: Someone fell for a painter who lives in the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to love someone dearly is to worship them.

clue.text: Decline to come to a terribly wild end

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly disordered

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to meet a dreadful, savage death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refuse, but it means to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink or diminish gradually is to fall away, a synonym.

clue.text: Endless surely, the revision of regulations

indicators.note: a revision reworks the remaining letters into a new order
endless means the final letter of the word is lopped off

explanation.surface: Surely the rulebook needs revising endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' removes the Y from SURELY, leaving SUREL, which 'revision' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulations are the laws or orders governing conduct, a synonym.

clue.text: Expatiates on vocal accompaniments

definitions.meaning: to expatiate is to talk at length on a subject
melodies sung above a main tune

explanation.walkthrough: To descant on a subject is to discourse at length; descants are also counter-melodies sung over a hymn tune.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means discoursing at length; as a noun, ornamental melodies sung above the main air.

clue.text: Symbolic of the Race of Man ?

definitions.text: Symbolic of the Race of Man ?

parts.words: Symbolic of the Race of Man ?
parts.note: the Isle of Man, home of the TT motorcycle race, has three running legs as its emblem

explanation.surface: Something representative of humanity as a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race of Man' sounds like humankind, but it is the TT race on the Isle of Man, whose emblem is three legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Having three feet or legs, like the Manx triskelion emblem.

clue.text: Outstanding items of daily concern'

parts.note: the most prominent pieces in a daily newspaper, where the paper states its own view on matters of concern

explanation.surface: A list of urgent jobs that need attending to every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A leading article is a newspaper editorial; 'outstanding' points to 'leading', and 'daily' is a daily paper rather than every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials are the pieces that lead a newspaper, so they are its prominent items.

clue.text: Diaphoretic applied to torso

definitions.meaning: a diaphoretic is a drug or agent that makes you perspire
a knitted jumper is worn on the upper body

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: something that makes you perspire, and a pullover worn over the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a perspiration-inducing agent; the other is a knitted pullover garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Potentially so adept a judge of Italian towns

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could potentially become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A capable magistrate oversees the towns of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: A podestà was the chief magistrate of a medieval Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: The podestà was the chief magistrate who ruled and judged in a medieval Italian city.

clue.text: He's present to protect the following of a craft

parts.note: being present means being here
to ward is to guard or protect

explanation.surface: A man stands by to guard the followers of some trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Saxon rebel Hereward was called 'the Wake', and a wake is the trail following a boat; 'craft' suggests a trade guild, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The English outlaw was known as 'the Wake', and a ship's wake is the water trailing behind it.

clue.text: Wipe out debt for a bit of joinery

parts.note: a mortise is the slot cut to receive a tenon in a joint

explanation.surface: A carpenter clears his debts with a piece of woodwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a loan gradually by instalments until it is cleared.

clue.text: King Edward caught a disease in Rye

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
got means caught, as of an illness

explanation.surface: A monarch fell ill while visiting the Sussex town of Rye.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye looks like the town in Sussex, but it is the cereal; the capital only disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal infection of rye and other grasses goes by this name.

clue.text: Preparation for laying down arms

definitions.meaning: soldiers ground arms by resting their weapons on the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground arms' is a drill command to lower rifles to the ground; a grounding is also a basic education.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic instruction prepares a learner, and the drill term means resting weapons on the earth.

clue.text: The fresh arrival being Thackeray's Colonel ? Right

parts.note: Colonel Newcome is the hero of Thackeray's novel The Newcomes

explanation.surface: A new character arrives, as the Colonel in Thackeray's novel did.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has just come on the scene is a recent entrant.

clue.text: Broken lease holds up artist's work

indicators.note: a lease that is broken has its letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement collapses and delays a painter's project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' reads as delays but means physically supports; the definition is a description of what the stand does.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand is the frame that props up a canvas in progress.

clue.text: Like Naaman before the cure, or Gehazi afterwards

definitions.text: Like Naaman before the cure, or Gehazi afterwards

parts.words: Like Naaman before the cure, or Gehazi afterwards
parts.note: in 2 Kings 5 the Syrian commander was healed of a skin disease, which then passed to Elisha's servant as punishment

explanation.surface: Describing two Old Testament figures before and after a healing.
explanation.walkthrough: Naaman was cured of leprosy by bathing in the Jordan; Elisha's servant Gehazi took his reward and was struck with the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflicted with the skin disease of the Bible, as both men were at different times.

clue.text: Oh! my — is a very Antony" (A and C.)

definitions.text: Oh! my — is a very Antony" (A and C.)

parts.words: Oh! my — is a very Antony" (A and C.)
parts.note: fill the gap in Cleopatra's line from Antony and Cleopatra, where she says she is all forgotten

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra (Act 1, scene 3) Cleopatra says 'O, my oblivion is a very Antony, And I am all forgotten.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quotation means forgetfulness, matching Cleopatra's following words about being forgotten.

clue.text: A bit of a blister, right out of minor poetry

indicators.note: out of signals the letter for right is removed from the word for minor poetry

parts.note: a versicle is a short verse

explanation.surface: A small poem stings like a blister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor poetry' sounds like a judgment of quality, but it is a versicle, a short verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sac of fluid, the kind that forms part of a blister on the skin.

clue.text: Sitting expected to become spirited

parts.note: a session where the sitters hope the spirits of the dead will appear

explanation.surface: A meeting that everyone hopes will liven up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' reads as lively but means visited by spirits, at a session to contact the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering to contact the dead; the French word means a sitting or session.

clue.text: Main location of pilots

parts.note: a main was a cockfighting match, held in a pit, and pilots fly from the forward compartment of a plane

explanation.surface: The chief base where aviators gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'chief', but a main is a cockfighting contest, held in a pit; the same word names the pilots' compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilots' cabin shares its name with the arena for cockfighting matches.

clue.text: Containers booked by Sherlock Holmes

definitions.meaning: Conan Doyle's last collection is The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes, so these are what the detective booked

explanation.walkthrough: The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes is the final collection of Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxes for holding things, and the detective's investigations collected in his Case-Book.

clue.text: Far and away the best means of conspicuity

definitions.text: Far and away the best means of conspicuity

parts.words: Far and away the best means of conspicuity
parts.note: the idiom 'conspicuous by one's not being there': being far away is the surest way to be noticed

explanation.surface: The finest way to make yourself stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far and away' reads as 'by a long way', but it means being far off and away, and the idiom says one is conspicuous by not being present.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'conspicuous by one's non-attendance' makes not being there the way to be noticed.

clue.text: Protective clothing for the stage

definitions.meaning: a garment tied over the front to keep clothes clean
the part of a theatre stage that projects in front of the curtain

explanation.walkthrough: An apron stage juts out into the audience in front of the proscenium.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore-like garment worn while cooking, and the forestage projecting before the curtain.

clue.text: Sugar and spice and all things nice, say ? That's getting it wrong

definitions.text: Sugar and spice and all things nice, say
definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme says this is what little girls are made of, so it is how a miss is constructed

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says little girls are made of 'sugar and spice and all things nice', so that recipe is a miss's construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A misreading or false interpretation; split as miss-construction it is also what a girl is made of.

clue.text: Object to nun's reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes the letters of the word for a nun

parts.note: a nun is a sister of a religious order

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a nun's efforts to reform her convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' hints at church history but is the anagram signal, applied to SISTER, the word for a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose or withstand something is to stand against it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Leading football teams are thus allied

definitions.meaning: the top clubs play inside the Football League
joined together in an alliance or conspiracy

explanation.walkthrough: Top clubs are 'in the league'; 'in league' also means working together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in alliance or collusion with someone; senior clubs also belong to a league competition.
